newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada board okays Amoco gas liquids project.
newsitem.headline: Canada board okays Amoco gas liquids project.

text.p: Canada's National Energy Board said on Thursday it approved Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd's plans to expand its natural gas liquids pipeline in southwestern Saskatchewan.

Amoco had applied to build a 155-km (96-mile) gas liquids pipeline extending to IPL Energy Inc's pipeline at Kerrobert, Saskatchewan from NGL extraction plants at Empress, Alberta at a cost of C$23 million.

The liquids pipeline transports all the NGLs from the Amoco, Empress Gas Liquids Joint Venture and the PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd extraction plants, and some of the liquids produced at a Petro-Canada plant.

The expansion, which would boost throughput by 49,920 barrels a day to 116,850 barrels a day, would twin an existing eight-inch pipeline to meet expected increases in NGL production from the Empress extraction facilities, located on the Alberta-Saskatchewan border, the NEB said.
The projected in-service date for the expanded facilities is November 1997.
